newsitem.title: USA: AOL slumps as investors overreact to 10-K.
newsitem.headline: AOL slumps as investors overreact to 10-K.

text.p: America Online Inc shares slumped on Tuesday as investors overreacted to the company's oft-repeated warnings that other online services and direct Internet access providers could spell tougher future competition.
Its shares fell four to 31-5/8 in heavy trading.

In a 10-K filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, AOL reiterated comments it made to analysts last quarter, warning of potentially high "churn" rates, the rate at which new customers join and quickly leave the service.

"(Investors) are significantly overreacting," said Abhishek Gami, an analyst for Nesbitt Burns. Other analysts also expressed surprise at the stock's fall, saying there was nothing new in the filing to merit such a fall.
"AOL may surprise all these people ... They have already confirmed the churn (rate) improved in this quarter and with the new marketing push, I'm convinced it will improve further," Gami said.
The company said yesterday it will spend over $100 million in a new marketing campaing to targeted to PC owners who are not current AOL members.

"A direct result of the campaign will be improved growth margins as AOL spends time giving away free hours and retains more experienced consumers, who provide higher margins. And AOL has said it is comfortable with quarterly and annual earnings views," Gami said. He said he expected the stock to rise as earnings period approaches.

America Online's is due to report earnings for the first fiscal quarter ended September 30, 1996 in late October or early November. It usually includes churn rate details in its quarterly announcements.
Other analysts echoed the sentiments. "There is no substance behind this," one analyst who declined to be identified said.
